stage_2_story.text_en:
Last Saturday, Moshe's favourite team, Hapoel Tel Aviv, played a crucial league match against Maccabi Haifa at a packed pitch in Tel Aviv. Moshe watched the match with his grandson Noam, who loves football and explained everything that happened.

The match began badly for Hapoel. In the fifth minute, their left back committed a reckless foul inside the penalty area. The referee had no hesitation — he pointed to the spot. Maccabi's captain stepped up and scored the penalty to make it one-nil.

Hapoel tried to respond. Their talented winger began to dribble past defenders, causing problems on the right side. However, every time Hapoel attacked, they were caught offside. The linesman raised his flag three times in the first half alone.

At half-time, Hapoel's coach changed the formation from four-four-two to four-three-three. He also brought on an experienced substitute — a tall striker known for winning headers from set pieces.

The change worked. In the sixty-eighth minute, the new striker rose above everyone and scored a powerful header from a corner kick. The equaliser brought the crowd to their feet.

The match ended one-all. Walking home, Moshe said to Noam: 'Football is never boring. Even when your team is losing, there is always hope.'

(c) He said in football there is always hope
(d) He said he would never watch football again
